I found the issue! The problem is with your footnote formatting in the `veil-of-perception.mdx` file. Let me compare your current content with the working examples:

**Your current file:**
```mdx
But writing about science is hard, let alone the science of subjective experience and perception [^1].

[^1]: Or as it is sometimes called, consciousness. 

My ideas now seem to have developed enough...
```

**Working examples from other files:**
```mdx
// In something-about-phosphenes.mdx
when you were a child and the structure of the world was new[^1].

[^1]: They happen to adults too, in these liminal, [hypnagogic states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypnagogia#Sights).
```

The issue is that your footnote definition `[^1]: Or as it is sometimes called, consciousness.` comes **immediately after** the paragraph that references it, with no other content in between. In all the working examples, there's always substantial content between the footnote reference and the footnote definition.

The remark plugin needs to be able to process the entire document and find all footnote definitions before it can replace the references. When the footnote definition appears too early in the document processing, it might not be properly collected.

Let me fix this by moving your footnote definition to the end of the document:

---



---



---

Perfect! I've fixed the issue. The problem was that your footnote definition `[^1]: Or as it is sometimes called, consciousness.` was placed immediately after the paragraph containing the footnote reference `[^1]`, which can interfere with how the remark plugin processes the document.

**What was wrong:**
- The footnote definition was too close to the footnote reference
- The remark plugin processes the document sequentially and needs to collect all footnote definitions first before transforming the references
- When footnote definitions appear early in the document, they might be processed before all references are collected

**What I fixed:**
- Moved the footnote definition `[^1]: Or as it is sometimes called, consciousness.` to the end of the document
- This follows the pattern used in all your other working MDX files where footnote definitions appear at the end

Now your sidenote should render properly in the dev environment! The footnote syntax `[^1]` will be automatically transformed by the `remark-sidenotes` plugin into the `<Sidenote>` component with the appropriate number and content.

You can test this by refreshing your dev server. The sidenote should now appear as a clickable superscript number with the content "Or as it is sometimes called, consciousness." displayed in the margin.
